info.title: Toolpath Engine API
info.description:
Public REST API for Toolpath engine operations.

**Waiting for a job.** Every operation that queues work answers `202` with a `jobId`.
Wait for it with **Stream job updates** (`GET /v1/jobs/{id}/events`), a server-sent event
stream that sends the job at once, sends it again on every change, and closes after
sending `succeeded` or `failed`. Both are final. An attempt exceeding its configured
deadline (default 300 seconds) fails without retry. Exhausted queue deliveries are
recovered by the worker from its DLQ, usually within a few minutes after the last
delivery with healthy consumers; outages delay recovery. A job still queued after
24 hours fails. Read the result as soon as the stream sends `succeeded`, and report the `error`
as soon as it sends `failed`. Do not wait by calling **Get a job** or a result endpoint in
a loop: a stream is one request however long the job runs, while a loop spends one request
of the key’s rate limit on every call. In a browser, read the stream with `fetch` and an
SSE parser: `EventSource` cannot send the `Authorization` header.

**Experimental.** Machining plans and toolpath calculation — creating, listing, and reading
plans, calculating toolpaths, and reading toolpath results and machining time — and
multi-body CAD files, under the `Files` tag, are experimental: available now but still
gaining functionality; planned additions include plan constraints and specifying material and
stock, among others. You can build against them today, but they may change substantially in a
minor release — reshaped, renamed, or removed — where the rest of the API keeps breaking
changes for a major version, apart from small ones with no material effect on clients. Every
breaking change is listed in the release notes, so check them before upgrading. Plan and
toolpath operations are grouped under the `Plans` and `Toolpaths` tags; every experimental
operation, field, and schema is marked `x-toolpath-experimental`.

**Units.** All dimensional values — in parts and in feature details — are in
millimetres; all angles are in degrees. Each part response also states this in its `units` field.

**Browser use.** CORS is per API key: a request only receives an
`Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header when its `Origin` is in the allowlist configured on the
key used (set when creating or editing the key in the portal). A key with no allowed origins
is server-to-server only. A Bearer API key placed in client-side JavaScript is readable by
anyone — restrict its origins, prefer a key granted read access only (writes made with it
are rejected with 403 `read_only_key`), or proxy requests through your own server.

**Access and billing.** An API key is granted read and write access separately in each area
of the API — the core API (uploads, part display, holders, and jobs), DFM (part analysis,
feature datasheets, and plans), and Quoting (toolpaths and machining time) — and that access
can be edited on an existing key in the portal. Every operation states its area in its
`x-toolpath-product` field (`core`, `dfm`, or `quoting`) and whether the call is billed in
`x-toolpath-metered`. Reads are free but still belong to their product: reading a plan needs
DFM access, and reading toolpaths needs Quoting. `GET` reads; every other method writes. A key
with no access to the operation’s area is refused with 403 `product_mismatch`; one with read
access used for a write is refused with 403 `read_only_key`.

ApiKeyAuth.description: A Toolpath API key supplied as a Bearer credential.

Turning.description: What reading the part for turning came to; narrow on `kind`.

frame.description: The axis it was read about.

areaFraction.description: The fraction of the part’s surface area lying on the outline within tolerance, from 0 to 1: what a lathe spinning the part here leaves finished.

turnability.description: The fraction of the outline’s revolved volume the part keeps, from 0 to 1. The rest is what turning leaves to be cut away some other way.

outline.description: The outline’s loops, each outer one followed by the inner loops inside it.

features.description: The outline’s features, in its order. A stretch both ends reach is listed twice, once per `approach`.

regionIdxsLeftForMilling.description: Indexes of the regions not wholly on the outline, ascending: what turning leaves for milling. A modeled thread’s regions are not among them.

featureTagsLeftForMilling.description: The milled features turning leaves for milling: each one with a region among `regionIdxsLeftForMilling`, whole, so a feature partly on the outline is listed. Join each value to `features[].featureTag`; the order is not meaningful.

TurningTurned.description: The part read about its turning axis.

AxisSource.description: Where the axis came from: `Detected` is the axis the part’s revolved surfaces agree on.

direction.description: The axis’s direction (unit length): the way z runs.

location.description: The point on the axis where z is 0, in mm. Purely radial: its projection onto the axis is zero.

radial.description: The way r runs, out from the axis (unit length).

TurningFrame.description: The half-plane a part is turned in: the axis, and how `(z, r)` lies in part coordinates — the point `location + z·direction + r·radial`.

r.description: Out from the axis, in mm.

OutlinePoint.description: A point of a turned part’s outline.

featureTag.description: Kernel turned-feature tag, encoded as a lowercase hexadecimal string. Stable across runs of one kernel version, not across versions. Hashed apart from a milled feature’s `featureTag`.

featureType.description: What it is, in snake_case (`od_groove`): its datasheet’s `featureType`, cased as a milled feature’s is. This vocabulary is open-ended.

approach.description: The end of the part it is cut from, whole: `PlusZ`, the end `frame.direction` points toward, or `MinusZ`, the other. A stretch both ends reach is two features, one per end, with the same `featureType` and `regionIdxs`. Null only on reports made before Engine API 1.29.0, for an `unknown` feature, which no cut reaches; absent on reports made before 1.26.0.

regionIdxs.description: Indexes of the regions it was spun from, ascending; join each value to `regions[].idx`.

datasheet.description: Its turning datasheet, or null when the analysis ran without feature details or where it could not be measured — and, on reports made before Engine API 1.29.0, for an `unknown` feature.

TurnedFeature.description: A stretch of a turned part’s outline, as cut from one end, and what it is.

AxialDirection.description: Which way along the axis something looks or comes from.

facts.description: What it measures, by kind; narrow on `facts.kind`.

zMin.description: Its start along the axis, in mm.

zMax.description: Its end along the axis, in mm.

rMin.description: Its nearest to the axis, in mm.

rMax.description: Its farthest from the axis, in mm.

mounting.description: How a tool must be mounted to reach it.

approach.description:
The end it is cut from, its feature's `approach`: an axial tool comes along the
axis from it, and a holder's hand feeds toward or away from the chuck at the other
end. The axial reach and the entry diameter are read from it.

slopeSpans.description:
**Experimental.** Available now and still gaining functionality. It may change in breaking ways in a minor API release; each such change is listed in the release notes, so check them before upgrading.

How steeply each of its curves rises and falls along a feed, in the order they run.

radialReachMinusZ.description:
**Experimental.** Available now and still gaining functionality. It may change in breaking ways in a minor API release; each such change is listed in the release notes, so check them before upgrading.

How deep a radial tool must reach, by how far toward −z from the feature the
material stands. Read off the finished part. A radial tool's holder trails its tip
to one side, so each side is read apart.

radialReachPlusZ.description:
**Experimental.** Available now and still gaining functionality. It may change in breaking ways in a minor API release; each such change is listed in the release notes, so check them before upgrading.

The same toward +z.

axialReach.description:
**Experimental.** Available now and still gaining functionality. It may change in breaking ways in a minor API release; each such change is listed in the release notes, so check them before upgrading.

The same for an axial tool coming from the end its feature is cut from, the
feature's `approach`, by how far across the axis from the feature the material
stands.

entryDiameter.description:
For a feature in a hole, the narrowest diameter between it and the end it is cut
from, in mm: what a bar entering from that end passes on its way in. Absent for any
other feature, or where nothing stands between.

minConcaveRadius.description:
The smallest radius of a concave corner between or on its curves, in mm, 0 for a
sharp one; absent where it has none.

axialStockToLeave.description: Material left along the spindle, in mm.

radialStockToLeave.description: Material left across the spindle, in mm.

toleranceBand.description: Permitted deviation bands for the turned feature.

TurningDatasheet.description:
One turned feature as a tool check sees it: the turning counterpart of a
`FeatureDatasheet`. In `(z, r)`, mm and degrees.

TurningNoAxis.description: The part’s revolved surfaces agree on no line, so it was not read.

kind.description: Discriminator: the axis was found but scored too low.

turnability.description: The part’s turnability about the axis found, from 0 to 1. Measured where the part was spun; where an estimate already fell well short of the threshold, that estimate, which reads low by at most a few hundredths.

TurningBelowThreshold.description: An axis was found, but the part’s turnability is under the default threshold.

kind.description: Discriminator: the part could not be read about its axis.

axis.description: The axis it was spun about.

error.description: What went wrong, for people to read. Its wording may change: branch on `code`.

code.description: The failure’s category, a stable code to branch on.

TurningSpinFailed.description: The part could not be spun about its axis, or its outline could not be read.

kind.description: Discriminator: no turning reading was asked for.

TurningNotRequested.description: No turning reading was asked for.

Turnability.description: Whether the part belongs on a lathe; narrow on `kind`.

kind.description: Discriminator identifying a part with no turning axis.
Discriminator identifying a part with a turning axis.

direction.description: Direction of the turning axis, as a unit vector.

location.description: Point on the turning axis, in mm. Purely radial: its projection onto the axis is zero.

areaFraction.description: Fraction of the part’s surface area a turning setup about this axis could finish, from 0 to 1 — the area lying on the part’s envelope of revolution within tolerance.

volumeFraction.description: Fraction of the part’s envelope of revolution — what comes off the lathe — that the part keeps, from 0 to 1. The rest is what a turning setup leaves to be cut away some other way, so a radially unbalanced part scores low here however much of its surface lies on the envelope.

jobId.description: Identifier of the queued processing job.

partId.description: Identifier of the part submitted for processing.

status.description: Initial state of the accepted processing job.

directions.description: Directions to analyze the part from beyond those the directions analysis chose — usually ones from the part’s `discoveredDirections`, passed back exactly as served, though any vector within 0.0001 of unit length is taken and normalized. They are added to the part for good: this analysis and every later one, and every plan and toolpath calculation, analyze the part from them too, so a `setupPlan` can state a setup in one and name its features. Each follows the part’s `candidateDirections` in the order added, and every feature the part had keeps its `featureTag`. A direction within 0.1° of one the part has adds nothing, and nor does one whose analysis fails; either is missing from the result’s `candidateDirections`. One within 0.1° of the exact opposite of a direction the part has is added as that exact opposite: read it back off `candidateDirections` rather than matching the direction sent. A part takes at most 12 added directions in all, and there is no removing one. Omit to analyze the part from the directions it has.

jobId.description: Identifier of the queued tessellation job.

partId.description: Identifier of the part submitted for tessellation.

fileId.description:
**Experimental.** Available now and still gaining functionality. It may change in breaking ways in a minor API release; each such change is listed in the release notes, so check them before upgrading.

Identifier of the file this part was made from, absent on a part uploaded on its own and once the file is deleted or pruned past the retention window.

bodyIndex.description:
**Experimental.** Available now and still gaining functionality. It may change in breaking ways in a minor API release; each such change is listed in the release notes, so check them before upgrading.

The `index` of the body of its file this part is: of the file it was made from, or the `bodyIndex` it was uploaded with. Absent on a part uploaded with none. It stays once the file is deleted or pruned, when `fileId` is absent.

reportId.description: Identifier of this immutable part result.

jobId.description: Identifier of the processing job that produced this part result.

kernelVersion.description: Version of the Toolpath kernel that produced this part result.

units.description: Units used by all dimensional values in this part response.

regions.description: Recognized B-rep regions, ordered by region index.

features.description: Features recognized during this processing run.

candidateDirections.description: Directions the part was analyzed from, and so the ones its features and a `setupPlan` can name: those the directions analysis chose, best first, then the added directions it could analyze the part from, in the order added.

discoveredDirections.description: Every direction detected on the part, best first — the axes of its holes and curved walls, the normals of its planes and the axes of its prisms, each both ways round. `candidateDirections` were chosen from these, and any other can be added to the part with **Analyze a part**: pass it back exactly as served. Null on part results made before this was recorded.

addedDirections.description: The directions this run was asked to analyze the part from beyond those the directions analysis chose: the part’s added directions when it was queued. One within 0.1° of the exact opposite of a direction the part has was added as that exact opposite, which `candidateDirections` holds in its place; any other missing from `candidateDirections` added nothing. Null on part results made before this was recorded.

directionZBounds.description: Part z extents for each candidate direction, or null when detail enrichment did not run.

turnability.description: How much of the part one turning setup could finish, or null when no reading was taken.

turning.description: What reading the part for turning came to, or null when no reading was taken. Narrow on `kind`.

meshTriangleCount.description: Number of triangles in the generated mesh.

meshStlUrl.description: 15-minute URL for the generated STL mesh, or null when absent.

meshGlbUrl.description: 15-minute URL for the generated GLB mesh, or null when absent.

angle.description: Unit used by every angular measurement.

splitOrigin.description: Part-local source-face group; equal values identify regions split from one B-rep face.

shapeKind.description: Recognized surface kind, such as Plane, Cylinder, Cone, Sphere, Torus, or Freeform.

area.description: Surface area of the region, in mm².

triangleStart.description: Inclusive start of this region’s triangle range in the returned mesh ordering.

triangleEnd.description: Exclusive end of this region’s triangle range in the returned mesh ordering.

featureId.description: Globally unique identifier of this feature record within its part result.

featureTag.description: Kernel feature tag, encoded as a lowercase hexadecimal string. Stable across runs of one kernel version, not across versions.

regionIdxs.description: Indexes of regions this feature covers; join each value to `regions[].idx`.

featureType.description: Kernel-recognized feature type. This vocabulary is open-ended as the kernel evolves.

machiningDirection.description: Access direction from which the kernel extracted this feature.

axis.description: Deprecated: use `machiningDirection`, which this repeats. Removed in the next API major.

direction.description: Candidate machining direction whose tool-axis frame defines these bounds.

zMin.description: Lowest part extent in this direction’s tool-axis frame, in mm.

zMax.description: Highest part extent in this direction’s tool-axis frame, in mm.

jobId.description: Identifier of the tessellation job that produced this display mesh.

meshPointCount.description: Number of points in the display mesh.

meshTriangleCount.description: Number of triangles in the display mesh.

faceTriangleCounts.description: How many of the mesh’s triangles each face of the body became, in mesh order. Every face is one contiguous span of triangles, so the counts partition the mesh and sum to `meshTriangleCount`: the first count’s triangles are the first face, the next count’s the second, and so on. Draw a line where two spans meet to outline the part. Null for a mesh tessellated before face spans were kept; queue a new tessellation to get them.

meshGlbUrl.description: 15-minute URL for the display mesh as binary glTF (GLB).

fileId.description: Identifier of the newly created file.

uploadUrl.description: Short-lived URL that accepts a direct upload of the CAD file.

sourceBucket.description: Object-storage bucket receiving the CAD file.

sourceS3Key.description: Object-storage key assigned to the CAD file.

jobId.description: Identifier of the queued inspection job.

fileId.description: Identifier of the file submitted for inspection.

status.description: Initial state of the accepted inspection job.

filename.description: The name the file was uploaded under.

createdAt.description: Time at which the file was created, in ISO 8601 format.

bodies.description: The file’s solid bodies, by `index`. Empty until an inspection has succeeded, and never changed after it: a file is inspected once, so an `index` names the same body for the life of the file.

shapes.description:
**Experimental.** Available now and still gaining functionality. It may change in breaking ways in a minor API release; each such change is listed in the release notes, so check them before upgrading.

The file’s distinct shapes, by the `index` of each one’s first body: separate copies of one shape are one entry, with a `count`. Empty until an inspection has succeeded.

hasMesh.description: Whether the inspection stored a display mesh of the bodies, served by **Get file mesh** (`GET /v1/files/{id}/mesh`). False before inspection, and after one whose meshing failed: meshing is best-effort, and the bodies are listed either way.

inspectJobId.description: Identifier of the inspection job that listed `bodies`, or null until one has succeeded.

index.description: Where the body is among the file’s solid bodies, from 0: what **Make parts from a file** names it by.

name.description: The body’s name, where the file gives it one.

faceCount.description: How many faces the body has as loaded.

lower.description: The box’s lowest corner, in mm.

upper.description: The box’s highest corner, in mm.

boundingBox.description: A box the body fits in, in mm in the file’s coordinates — not necessarily the tightest.

shape.description:
**Experimental.** Available now and still gaining functionality. It may change in breaking ways in a minor API release; each such change is listed in the release notes, so check them before upgrading.

The shape this body is: the `index` of the lowest-indexed body of the file it matches, in any position and orientation, and its own `index` when it is the first. Bodies are matched on volume, surface area, face count, mass distribution and handedness, not exact geometry, so some different bodies match: a hole pattern rotated on a symmetric plate, or a near-symmetric part and its mirror image. One part of a shape can be quoted by its `count`.

index.description: The shape’s first body, which stands for every copy: the one **Make parts from a file** takes.

bodies.description: Every body of the file that matches this shape, by `index`, ascending. A match is by mass properties, not exact geometry, so check it before quoting from it.

count.description: How many of this shape one of the file’s assemblies needs: what a quote multiplies by. Today one for each of its `bodies`. A body an assembly places more than once is still listed once, and counted once, until placements are reported.

FileShape.description:
**Experimental.** Available now and still gaining functionality. It may change in breaking ways in a minor API release; each such change is listed in the release notes, so check them before upgrading.

One shape of a file, and how many it needs.

jobId.description: Identifier of the inspection job that produced this display mesh.

meshGlbUrl.description: 15-minute URL for the display mesh of every body as binary glTF (GLB), one node per body.

bodyIndex.description: The `index` of the body the part is.

created.description: Whether this request made the part. False when the body was already made a part, which is then the part returned: one body of a file is only ever one part.

shape.description: The shape the body is, as `GET /v1/files/{id}` lists it: its first body, every body that is it, and its `count`. Information only — a part made of one body of a shape can be quoted by the shape's `count` rather than made once per copy.

parts.description: One part for each body named, in the order named.

bodies.description: The bodies to make parts of, each named once by its `index` among the file’s `bodies`, at most 100 to a call. Any body may be named, a copy of another shape included.

jobId.description: Identifier of the queued enrichment job.

partId.description: Identifier of the part owning the requested features.

status.description: Initial state of the accepted enrichment job.

featureIds.description: Identifiers of features from one part whose detailed machining data should be generated.

datasheets.description: Detailed machining data for requested features.

notFound.description: Requested feature identifiers that were unknown.

featureTag.description: Kernel feature tag, encoded as a lowercase hexadecimal string. Stable across runs of one kernel version, not across versions.

featureType.description: Kernel-recognized feature type; the vocabulary is open-ended.

datasheet.description: Generated machining detail, or null when this feature has no detail yet.

featureType.description: Kernel-recognized feature type that this datasheet measures.

zMin.description: Bottom of the feature along the tool axis, in mm.

zMax.description: Top of the feature along the tool axis, in mm.

extendedZMin.description:
Bottom of the band a pass over the feature reaches, in mm: `zMin`, or lower where a
chamfer on the far edge of a through feature deepens it. This, not `zMin`, is where
a wall pass and the whole-part rough run out, the reach a tool is held to, and the
depth the time estimates and setup planning read.

extendedZMax.description:
Top of the band a pass over the feature runs down, in mm: `zMax`, or higher where a
chamfer, fillet or countersink sits on the feature's mouth. This, not `zMax`, is where
a rough, a wall pass and a hole's helix start, the reach a tool is held to, and the top
of the band the time estimates read.

reachCurve.description: How deep a tool must reach, by how far outboard of the cut the material stands.

axialStockToLeave.description: Material intentionally left along the tool axis for a later operation, in mm.

radialStockToLeave.description: Material intentionally left radially for a later operation, in mm.

toleranceBand.description: Permitted deviation bands for the machined feature.

hasFloor.description: Whether the feature has a floor machined perpendicular to the tool axis.

hasWall.description: Whether the feature has a wall machined parallel to the tool axis.

projectedFloorArea.description: Projected area machined floor-wise (perpendicular to the tool axis).

floorishArea.description: Deprecated: use `projectedFloorArea`. Removed in the next API major.

projectedWallArea.description: Area machined wall-wise (parallel to the tool axis).

wallishArea.description: Deprecated: use `projectedWallArea`. Removed in the next API major.

areas.description: What the surface is made of, as a partition that sums to the feature's area.

pinchPoints.description:
The places the feature is at its tightest: where the clearance reaches the minimum
`cd` reports, one point per place, in part coordinates, tightest first and never more
than ten.

The counterpart of a bound rather than another bound: what these answer is *where*
the clearance minimum was decided, which the number itself cannot. A drawing is the
audience, which is why the list is capped — a feature can tie in dozens of places,
and the eleventh point tells a reader nothing the first ten did not.

Read off the medial axis where the clearance was measured against a single one. Beyond
that: a hole is pointed at on its axis at the top of its wall; a dovetail, whose
minimum is the smallest cutter spanning its undercut, once along each run of its
overhangs' foot; an inside corner with no radius that zeroed the minimum, whatever the
kind; a layered kind's minimum that is the widest tool reaching all of it — a ball, a
bullnose or a flat — where a wider one is stopped or the surface bends too tightly for
it; and a layered kind's minimum read off one of its slices (a chamfer's), on that slice.
Empty where the minimum is unbounded (a facing pass) or its measurement failed, where a
dovetail's foot could not be read, and where a layered kind's minimum is none of these. Empty is "nowhere to point at", never
"nowhere is tight".

FeatureDatasheet.description:
One feature as machining sees it: static, self-contained, and enough to choose a tool against without having the part in hand. All lengths mm and angles degrees, in the tool frame of the direction the feature is machined from, whose origin is the part’s own: z runs up the tool axis, so `zMin` is the bottom of the feature and `zMax` its top. A pinch point’s `point` and a surface’s `minCurvatureDiameterAt` are the exceptions, in part coordinates.

Every number in it is finite, so it survives a JSON round trip. A limit nothing sets is `null`, so that every value passes it, except where a field’s description says it is absent instead. Any other field that is omitted has no value to read.

jobId.description: Identifier of the queued processing job.

partId.description: Identifier of the part submitted for processing.

planId.description: Identifier of the plan this job writes to. Read results at /plans/{planId} once the job completes.

material.description: The material the job was planned for — the request’s, or the default when it named none. Echoed so the choice is visible even when a non-JSON body dropped it.

toolCrib.description: The tool crib the job was planned with — the request’s, or the default when it named none — as validated.

machine.description: The machine the job was recorded against — the request’s, or null when it named none — and whose `maxRpm` its tools are held under.

setupPlan.description: The setup plan the job extends — the request’s, or null for the kernel’s own plan.

doneRegions.description: The regions the job treats as done — the request’s, or null for none.

input.description: The stock policy the job cuts from, all lengths mm, with omitted figures left omitted. The request’s stock policy, or the saved input on a recalculation, or automatic Flat Bar on a new plan and a plan made before stock inputs were recorded. A recalculation without stock reuses this.

resolved.description: Always null: not calculated yet. Read the plan after the job succeeds.

stock.description: The queued stock input and its not-yet-calculated geometry.

fallbackTools.description: Whether the job plans what the crib cannot with fallback tools.

workholding.description: How the job holds the part — the request’s, or `thinAir` when it named none.

status.description: Initial state of the accepted processing job.

mode.description: Flat Bar: a block sized around the part.

oversizeX.description: Minimum material on each side of the part along setup x, mm. Default 0.762 (0.03").

oversizeY.description: Minimum material on each side of the part along setup y, mm. Default 0.762 (0.03").

oversizeZTop.description: Minimum material above the part, mm. Default 0.762 (0.03").

oversizeZBottom.description: Grip stock: exact material below the part, mm. Default 6.35 (1/4").

snapX.description: Width rounding increment, mm; 0 leaves it unrounded. Default 6.35 (1/4").

snapY.description: Depth rounding increment, mm; 0 leaves it unrounded. Default 6.35 (1/4").

snapZ.description: Thickness rounding increment, mm; 0 leaves it unrounded. Default 6.35 (1/4").

AutomaticFlatBarStock.description: Automatic Flat Bar: a block sized around the part. Omitted figures take the default; each is at most 762 mm (30 in). The block that comes to must fit 2032 × 1270 mm across the cutting direction and 762 mm along it, or the job fails.

mode.description: Round Stock: a cylinder sized around the part.

radialOversize.description: Minimum material around the part’s smallest enclosing circle, mm. Default 0.762 (0.03").

axialOversize.description: Front oversize: minimum material past the part’s far end, along the bar, mm. Default 0.762 (0.03").

gripStock.description: Exact material between the bar’s base and the part’s near end, mm. Default 6.35 (1/4").

diaRoundToNearest.description: Diameter rounding increment, mm; 0 leaves it unrounded. Default 6.35 (1/4").

lengthRoundToNearest.description: Length rounding increment, mm; 0 leaves it unrounded. Default 6.35 (1/4").

verticalAxis.description: Stand the bar along the first setup’s cutting direction instead of laying it along the part’s long side. Default false: lying down.

AutomaticRoundStock.description: Automatic Round Stock: a cylinder lying along the part’s long side — or with `verticalAxis`, standing along the first setup’s cutting direction — centered on the part’s smallest enclosing circle about that axis and sized around it. Omitted figures take the default; each is at most 762 mm (30 in). The bar that comes to must fit within 2032 × 1270 × 762 mm in some order as diameter × diameter × length, or the job fails.

FixedCylinderStock.description: A cylinder of given size, standing along the first setup’s cutting direction and centered on the part’s smallest enclosing circle. Its box, diameter × diameter × length, must fit within 80 × 50 × 30 in (2032 × 1270 × 762 mm) in some order.

mode.description: Another body of the part’s own file.

BodyStock.description:
**Experimental.** Available now and still gaining functionality. It may change in breaking ways in a minor API release; each such change is listed in the release notes, so check them before upgrading.

Another solid body of the part’s own file, taken where it lies — a casting, a forging, or what an earlier operation left — never sized or squared up. The part must stand inside it, or the job fails. Regions of the part the body already leaves at their final surface are skipped: no setup machines them. Only a part made from a file can be cut from one.

shape.description: A block: tells it from a `cylinder`.

location.description: The frame’s origin, in part coordinates, mm.

refDirection.description: Its x axis, unit length and square to `axis`.

lower.description: The block’s lower corner, in `frame`, mm.

upper.description: The block’s upper corner, in `frame`, mm.

shape.description: A bar: tells it from a `box`.

origin.description: The cylinder’s base center, in part coordinates, mm.

axis.description: Unit vector from the base along the bar, in part coordinates: the first setup’s cutting direction for an upright bar, the part’s long side for one lying down.

length.description: Cylinder length along its axis, mm.

shape.description: A body of the part’s file.

bodyIndex.description: The stock body’s index among the part’s file’s `bodies`.

materialFreeRegions.description: The part’s regions (indices into its report’s `regions`) the stock body already leaves at their final surface, ascending. The plan skips them: no setup machines them.

StockBody.description:
**Experimental.** Available now and still gaining functionality. It may change in breaking ways in a minor API release; each such change is listed in the release notes, so check them before upgrading.

Initial stock taken where it lies: another body of the part’s own file, never sized or squared up, so no figure is reported — the body is the figure.

material.description: The material to synthesize tools and machining times for. Omit for aluminium, the default.

toolCrib.description: Where tools come from: a tool crib of one to sixteen tool libraries, in priority order — each pass of the plan uses the first library with a tool for it. Each library has a `kind`; today the only kind is `implicit`, a library whose tools are synthesized from settings (explicit libraries of catalog tools will follow). An implicit library has an optional `name` (a label) and enables tool families (faceMill, flatEndmill, bullNose, ballEndmill, drill, chamfer, keyseat, tap, cornerRounding), and each family has its own settings for inch-sized tools and for metric ones — a face mill diameter, diameter ranges and a maximum length-over-diameter, in millimetres; any setting left out takes its default. A family left out is not made, and planning falls back where it can: without drills, holes are milled; without a face mill, facing uses a flat endmill; without chamfer mills, bevels are followed by a bullnose, then a ball. Endmill `minDiameter` is a hard minimum. Inch drills are the fractional, number and letter series, and metric drills the metric series; a library enabling both makes the nearest stocked size of either, one drill per hole, unless its two blocks state different `maxLengthOverDiameter`, when each system's drills are made separately. A drill block that states no `maxDiameter` stocks its whole series, to 4 1/4" and 57 mm. Corner-rounding diameters are the whole cutter. `tap` is every tool that cuts a thread — cutting and forming taps, and thread mills — each made only for a threaded hole or stud of the process its thread names, a tap at a standard thread size. A stud’s thread is milled, so with `tap` off every stud is planned without its thread. A thread with no tool for it is planned without its thread, which is reported owed. Omit for one implicit library with every family inch-sized at its defaults, corner rounders off, and drills in both systems with `maxDiameter` stated at 50.8 (2") and 50 — a part's units are not known before it is uploaded, so a hole takes the nearest stocked drill of either.

machine.description: The machine the part is quoted on: `name`, `maxRpm` (the spindle's top speed, rev/min) and `toolChangeSeconds`. Recorded with the plan and echoed back, and carried over by a recalculation. `maxRpm` is applied: every synthesized tool is held under it, so machining times move for a machine that states one; without it a default ceiling of 15000 rev/min applies. Tool changes are never included in machining times; `toolChangeSeconds` is for the caller to price them. Omit for none.

setupPlan.description: The setup plan to extend: setups in machining order, each stated as one `orientations` entry — a setup machines from one direction — naming the features (`featureTag`, hex) to machine from its `direction`. A direction must be one of the part’s `candidateDirections` — the kernel’s choice, or one added with **Analyze a part** — passed back exactly as served (a unit vector), and a feature is named under its own direction. The plan made keeps these setups first, in this order, each holding at least the features named (and every other offered feature of its direction), and appends setups where the part needs more. A plan read serves its own `setupPlan`, which can be edited and sent back. Tags are stable only within one `kernelVersion`. A feature named is machined where it is named whatever it needs: one no tool in the crib cuts is planned all the same, its passes left `unmachined`. It also keeps its regions from every other feature, in every direction: a feature that shares one is planned as what is left of it, under a tag of its own that the plan’s `trimmedFeatures` describes, and the plan’s `setupPlan` may name that tag in turn. A statement the kernel cannot honor fails the job, whose `error` begins `refused_user_plan:` and gives one clause per refused statement. Omit or null for the kernel’s own plan; on **Calculate a plan’s toolpaths**, omit to keep the plan’s statement and null to clear it.

doneRegions.description: Regions already at their final surface — near-net stock, a face finished before the part arrives: `regions`, indices into the part report’s `regions`, and the `kernelVersion` of the report they were read from. Region indices are stable only within one kernel release, so a job planned by another fails, its `error` beginning `stale_regions:`; an index the part does not have fails it as `unknown_regions:`. A done region is left out of the plan’s `issues`, its machining times and its toolpaths, and no feature planned holds one: a part feature that does is planned as what is left of it, under a tag of its own that the plan’s `trimmedFeatures` describes, and one whose regions are all done is not planned. A `setupPlan` may still name such a feature by its part-report tag: what is left of it is stated in its place. A done region on the top of a direction turns off facing from that direction, and the part’s other top faces are machined one by one. The stock is unchanged: it is still the block around the part, so the simulation cuts air over a done region. Omit or null for none; on **Calculate a plan’s toolpaths**, omit to keep the plan’s and null to clear them.

stock.description: Initial stock settings. Omit stock to use automatic Flat Bar on a new plan or keep the saved input on a recalculation. The initial stock to cut from, all lengths mm, told apart by `mode`: automatic Flat Bar or Round Stock sized around the part, a fixed block or cylinder placed against it, or another body of the part’s own file. Omit it on a new plan for automatic Flat Bar at the default figures; omit it when recalculating a plan to reuse that plan’s own.

fallbackTools.description: Plan what the tool crib cannot. A pass no tool of the crib can play — a hole deeper than its drills reach, a pocket past its endmills’ `maxLengthOverDiameter`, a head no library lists — is given a tool from a last, fallback tier with the reach limits lifted, so the part has a time for it. The crib comes first: a pass any crib tool can play keeps that tool. Each fallback tool is marked `outsideCrib` on the plan’s actions, with why the crib had none. Omit or false for today’s plans, which leave such passes `unmachined`. Not carried by a recalculation: state it on each request that wants it.

workholding.description: How the part is held. `thinAir`, the default, holds it by nothing: the optimistic answer, since a fixture only ever takes reach away. `syntheticVise` holds it in a vise sized to whatever it closes on, its jaws along each setup’s y, so a jaw blocks the reach it would. The first setup grips the initial stock, every later setup the part as cut; the jaws reach 5.35 mm up whatever they close on, at most half its height. The planner chooses the first setup among the directions the stock can be gripped in. Fixed stock is gripped only in the directions the part fits it squared up in; where it fits in none — or not in the direction a `setupPlan` states its first setup in — the job fails, its `error` beginning `part_outside_initial_stock:` and naming each direction. A job no first setup can start otherwise fails, its `error` beginning `invalid_argument: setup planning: no fixture on the initial stock holds a first setup`; a `setupPlan` whose first setup cannot start fails as `refused_user_plan:`. Faces a jaw leaves out of reach are reported as the plan’s `issues`. Omit on **Calculate a plan’s toolpaths** to keep the plan’s.

items.description: The part’s plans in this page, newest first.

pageSize.description: Maximum number of plans returned in this page.

total.description: Total number of plans for this part.

jobId.description: Identifier of the job that produced this plan.

kernelVersion.description: Version of the Toolpath kernel that produced this plan.

material.description: The material this plan was synthesized for. Its tools’ feeds and speeds — and so every machining time here — are the kernel’s for it. `Aluminum` on plans made before it was recorded.

level.description: Fidelity of this plan: `planned` (setups and action-specs only) or `toolpathed` (toolpaths also calculated). See PlanResponse.level for when a plan is readable at `planned`.

issues.description: The plan’s coverage shortfalls (see PlanResponse.issues). Empty when it covers all.

kind.description: How the plan falls short: `Unseen` (regions no direction reaches at all), `OutOfPlay` (regions some direction reaches but no feature in play holds — one the kernel rejected or excluded, or one left out because it would not measure) or `Incomplete` (regions some feature could reach that the plan leaves untouched).

area.description: Faceted area of this shortfall, in mm² — the figure to gate a quote on.

regionCount.description: How many part regions this shortfall covers.

PlanIssueSummary.description: A plan’s coverage shortfall, as a plan list states it.

jobId.description: Identifier of the job that produced this plan. A toolpath calculation records itself here as soon as it has planned the part, while it cuts; a `toolpathed` plan keeps the job of its last result until a recalculation completes. Compare it with the job you queued.

kernelVersion.description: Version of the Toolpath kernel that produced this plan.

material.description: The material this plan was synthesized for. Its tools’ feeds and speeds — and so every machining time here — are the kernel’s for it. `Aluminum` on plans made before it was recorded.

input.description: The stock policy the job cuts from, all lengths mm, with omitted figures left omitted. The request’s stock policy, or the saved input on a recalculation, or automatic Flat Bar on a new plan and a plan made before stock inputs were recorded. A recalculation without stock reuses this.

resolved.description: The initial stock the kernel sized and placed, in mm, told apart by `shape`: a `box` — two corners in the first setup’s frame, squared up in the direction the job cuts first — a `cylinder` in part coordinates, or the `body` of the part’s file it was cut from. This is the material bought, which a quote is written against (a cylinder’s volume is π·(diameter/2)²·length); the part’s own bounding box is not a substitute. Null for a plan calculated before this field existed — re-run the part to get one — and for a part with no setup, which has nothing to square stock against.

stock.description: The saved stock input and the initial geometry the kernel resolved from it.

workholding.description: How the plan’s job held the part, which a recalculation that names none holds it by. `thinAir` for plans made before Engine API 1.24.0.

level.description: Fidelity of this plan: `planned` (setups and action-specs only) or `toolpathed` (toolpaths also calculated — fetch them at /plans/{planId}/toolpaths). A plan is readable at `planned` as soon as a calculation has planned the part, while `jobId` names the job cutting it. A `toolpathed` plan keeps its last result while it is recalculated. After a failed calculation the plan stays as its last successful run left it, or `planned` under the failed job.

issues.description: The plan’s coverage shortfalls — what it leaves uncut, each with its area (mm²). Empty when the plan machines everything it owes; gate a quote on this rather than on cut coverage alone.

setupPlan.description: The plan’s own statement of itself, in the shape a request’s `setupPlan` takes: every setup in order, its direction, and the features planned from it. Sent back with the same `doneRegions`, tool crib, material and machine, under the same `kernelVersion`, it plans the same, so it is what a caller edits to restate the plan. Its tags belong to this plan’s `kernelVersion`. Null for a plan with no setup and for plans made before it was recorded.

doneRegions.description: The regions this plan was told are already at their final surface, and the kernel version they were read under — or null for none. They are left out of `issues`, of machining times and of toolpaths: a plan whose `issues` are empty machines everything it owes *except* these, which the caller vouched for.

trimmedFeatures.description: The features of the part as this plan reads it — after its skipped regions and stated features trim it — that `GET /v1/parts/{id}` does not list, whether or not a setup names them. A part feature holding a region the plan skips — a done region, or one its stock body already leaves at size — or a region of a feature the job’s `setupPlan` names, is read as what is left of it, under a tag of its own, which the plan’s `setupPlan`, `featureTags` and `unmachined` may name; each such feature is here, with the part feature it was cut from. Empty where nothing trimmed a feature; null for a plan that skips no region and whose `setupPlan` names no feature, and for plans made before Engine API 1.30.0.

kind.description: How the plan falls short: `Unseen` (regions no direction reaches at all), `OutOfPlay` (regions some direction reaches but no feature in play holds — one the kernel rejected or excluded, or one left out because it would not measure) or `Incomplete` (regions some feature could reach that the plan leaves untouched).

area.description: Faceted area of this shortfall, in mm² — the figure to gate a quote on.

regionCount.description: How many part regions this shortfall covers.

features.description: For an `OutOfPlay` shortfall, the features holding its regions that were never in play, and why. A region can be held by several features. Empty for `Unseen`, whose regions no feature holds. Absent for `Incomplete`, on every issue of a plan whose features could not be read (its issues are stated without them), and on plans made before this was recorded.

unattributedRegionCount.description: How many of this shortfall’s regions no feature in `features` holds: all of them for `Unseen`. A sliver held only by an edge break’s dead stop counts here, and so does a region held only by a feature the plan never measured, because it could do without it. Absent where `features` is.

featureTag.description: Kernel feature tag (hex), as `PlanSetup.unmachined` states one — join to a part feature’s `featureTag` (from `GET /v1/parts/{id}`) or to the plan’s `trimmedFeatures`.

cause.description: Why no setup machines it. `ToolsRefused`: no tool of the plan can cut it, so it was never offered to the planner. `Revoked`: it shares regions with a pocket-like feature of another direction, which must be machined as that pocket. `RefusesEveryTool`: its own measurement admits no tool at all. `MeasurementFailed`: its clearance measurement failed. `FallbackNotNeeded`: only a fallback tool cuts it, and other features machine every region it would with the tool crib alone, so the plan does without it (`fallbackTools`). `Unmeasured`: the plan’s reading of it would not measure, so nothing is known of it. Other values may be added.

owed.description: The passes no tool of the plan meets — `Rough`, `Finish` or `Thread` — in that order. Empty where the tools meet every pass, or nothing is known of it (`Unmeasured`).

rejections.description: For `ToolsRefused`, why no tool was invented for those passes, each reason once: the tool crib’s reasons, or with `fallbackTools`, the reasons no fallback tool could be made, reach lifted. They are the kernel’s rejection codes, such as `ClearanceAtSharpCorner`, `DiameterTooSmall`, `FluteLengthTooLong`, `StickoutTooLong`, `LengthOverDiameterTooHigh`, `CannotSynthesizeDrill`, `ToolTypeExcluded` or `MeasurementFailed`, and for a `Thread` pass `ThreadNotOnGrid`, `ThreadTapered`, `ThreadEntryObstructed`, `ThreadLeadTooLong` or `TeethLengthTooLong`; other values may be added. Empty when the crib lists no tool head and `fallbackTools` is off; empty for any other cause.

PlanIssueFeature.description: A feature holding regions of a plan issue, and why no setup machines it.

idx.description: Position of this item in machining order.

direction.description: The setup’s machining direction (tool axis), or null when none is exposed.

unmachined.description: Feature tags (hex) this setup was meant to machine that its passes leave short: a feature no pass cuts, or one roughed but owed its finish, such as a hole drilled under size where no stocked drill lands in its tolerance. Empty when the setup machines everything assigned.

idx.description: Position of this item in machining order.

intent.description: What kind of pass this action is, as tp-kernel states it. Coarser than the pass’s concrete strategy, which the kernel keeps to itself: a whole-part rough reads `AdaptiveRough`, and a drill finish, a facing pass, an undercut and a chamfer all read `Finish`.

toolName.description: Name of the tool this action uses.

featureTags.description: Feature tags (hex) this action is for — join to a part feature’s `featureTag` (from `GET /v1/parts/{id}`), or, for a feature the plan’s skipped regions trimmed, to the plan’s `trimmedFeatures`. Whole-part roughing names the features its sweep folds in and facing the faces it takes; plans computed before this was recorded list none for either.

tool.description: The full synthesized tool spec, or null when the kernel exposes none. Its `key` names the tool within this plan only: two actions with equal keys run in one tool, so a change of key between consecutive actions is a tool change. It is not an identity across plans or kernel versions, and is absent on plans computed before tp-kernel 0.10.0. It gained `fluteCount` and `stickout` (the tool’s reach below its holder, mm) in tp-kernel 0.14.0, both absent on plans made before it. A tap or thread mill carries the thread it cuts: `threadPitch` (mm), a tap its `threadHandedness`, and its form `threadProfileDeg` (the included flank angle) and taper `threadTaperDeg` (the half angle of the pitch cone, 0 for a straight thread), these two absent on plans made before Engine API 1.23.0. Chip load is `cuttingFeedRate / (spindleSpeed × fluteCount)`; surface speed is `π × diameter × spindleSpeed / 1000` (m/min). A tool made past the tool crib, for a pass no crib tool could play (a job asked for `fallbackTools`), carries `outsideCrib: { reasons }`: the kernel’s reasons no crib tool fit this pass’s features — `LengthOverDiameterTooHigh`, `ToolTypeExcluded`, … — each once, possibly none.

feedSpeed.description: What this action runs at — spindle speed, cutting feed and the step depths — or null. Null covers two cases the plan’s `kernelVersion` tells apart: the action’s tool has no feeds for the pass, or the plan was computed before tp-kernel 0.14.0 and carries none at all.

stepdown.description: The most a layer may take, in mm, where the pass sets one.

stepover.description: The stepover the pass is calculated with, in mm, where the pass sets one; on a countersink spiral, the most it steps.

featureTag.description: Kernel feature tag (hex) the plan reads this feature under. `GET /v1/parts/{id}` lists no feature under it.

featureType.description: What the rest of the part feature reads as, in snake_case as a part feature’s `featureType` is: a pocket whose floor is done may read as a wall. This vocabulary is open-ended.

machiningDirection.description: Access direction from which the kernel extracted this feature, as on a part feature: that of the part feature it was cut from.

regionIdxs.description: Indexes of the regions it holds, ascending; join each value to the part report’s `regions[].idx`. None is a region the plan skips.

fromFeatureTag.description: The `featureTag` of the part feature it was cut from, which holds every one of its regions, and also the ones cut away from it. Null where no one part feature does.

TrimmedFeature.description: A feature of the part as a plan reads it that the part report does not list, whether or not a setup names it: what the plan’s skipped regions (done, or left at size by its stock body), or the features its `setupPlan` names, left of a part feature, which the kernel reads again on the rest of its regions under a tag of its own.

jobId.description: Identifier of the job that produced these toolpaths.

kernelVersion.description: Version of the Toolpath kernel that produced these toolpaths.

initialStockUrl.description: 15-minute URL for the exact initial stock mesh (GLB, part coordinates, mm), before the first action. Null when unavailable; fall back to the plan’s stock.resolved figure. A plain GLB, like `meshGlbUrl`: no glTF extension is needed to read it. It is stored gzipped and served with `Content-Encoding: gzip` whatever the request’s `Accept-Encoding`: browsers and `fetch` undo that on their own, but curl without `--compressed`, wget, Python’s `urllib`, and Java’s and .NET’s HTTP clients by default hand back the gzipped bytes, which must be gunzipped before the GLB is parsed.

camExportUrl.description: 15-minute URL for the CAM export: a zip another CAM system rebuilds this job from in its own operations. `job.json` states the tools, the features, the setups in machining order and each action as its intent, tool, heights, feeds and the strategy the plan decided, a refused action with its reason; beside it are the part and the faces each action machines as STEP, and each calculated action’s toolpath as binary columns. Its format may change in any release. Null for a plan calculated before 1.37.0, and where the export is unavailable — one of its toolpaths tilts the tool, which it cannot state. **Experimental.** Available now and still gaining functionality. It may change in breaking ways in a minor API release; each such change is listed in the release notes, so check them before upgrading.

Whole-part roughing names the features its sweep folds in and facing the faces it takes; plans computed before this was recorded list none for either.

machiningTime.description: Machining time for this action from the cut toolpath’s programmed feeds (links and rapids included, tool change excluded), in seconds, or null when the action was refused.

cuttingLength.description: Cutting-motion length of the toolpath in mm, or null when the action was refused.

pathLength.description: Full toolpath length including links and rapids, in mm, or null when the action was refused.

empty.description: True when the runner ran this action but it produced no cutting motion (nothing left to cut) — distinct from a real cut and from a refusal. Its machining time and lengths are zero and no geometry is stored. Always false for a refused action or a plan that is only `planned`.

feedSpeed.description: What this action runs at — spindle speed, cutting feed and the step depths — or null. Null covers two cases the plan’s `kernelVersion` tells apart: the action’s tool has no feeds for the pass, or the plan was computed before tp-kernel 0.14.0 and carries none at all.

refusedReason.description: Why the runner refused to cut this action, or null when it cut. It begins with a code: `refused_pass:` for a pass not cut against the stock as it stands, or past its cutting-time limit; `timed_out:` for a calculation stopped at its time limit; `unsupported:` for a pass nothing can cut yet; `invalid_argument:` for a pass that cannot be cut as given, such as one whose tool has no feeds for it; `internal:` for a fault in the calculation. An action of a plan whose `kernelVersion` is earlier than 0.29.0 may begin `geometry:` instead. Codes may be added in any release.

toolpathUrl.description: 15-minute URL for the toolpath geometry, or null when the action was refused, empty, or its geometry is unavailable. The file is JSON: `points`, xyz triples in part coordinates, and `sections`, the path in order. A section is the points from `start` up to `end` (exclusive), counted in points, not numbers; each after the first starts with a copy of the point before it, and one may be empty. Its `kind` is `Cutting`, `Approach`, `LeadIn`, `ConnectionNotClearanceArea`, `ConnectionClearanceArea`, `LeadOut` or `Retract`; kinds may be added in any release, so read an unknown one as a link. A file written before 1.38.0 has no `sections`. `segments` is deprecated: the same ranges, with every kind but `Cutting`, `LeadIn` and `LeadOut` a `RapidMove`. A file written before 1.18.0 also carries a `frame`, and its points are in that frame: place them through it.

stockAfterUrl.description: 15-minute URL for the in-process stock after this action (GLB, part coordinates, mm). Null for a refused or empty action, or an unavailable artifact. Fall back to the preceding available stock mesh in machining order, then initialStockUrl, then the plan’s stock.resolved figure. A plain GLB, like `meshGlbUrl`: no glTF extension is needed to read it. It is stored gzipped and served with `Content-Encoding: gzip` whatever the request’s `Accept-Encoding`: browsers and `fetch` undo that on their own, but curl without `--compressed`, wget, Python’s `urllib`, and Java’s and .NET’s HTTP clients by default hand back the gzipped bytes, which must be gunzipped before the GLB is parsed.

requiredStep.description: The pipeline step that must run before this data is available.

jobStatus.description: State of the latest job for the required step: queued or running when one is in progress, failed when the last attempt failed, or null when no such job has been queued for this part.

kernelVersion.description: Version of the Toolpath kernel that produced these toolpaths.

totalMachiningTimeSeconds.description: Sum of every cut action’s calculated machining time, in seconds — the toolpath time at its programmed feeds (links and rapids included), with tool changes excluded and refused actions contributing nothing, so when `refusedCount` is nonzero this total is partial (not the whole job).

refusedCount.description: Number of actions the runner refused (no toolpath calculated). These contribute nothing to the totals, so a nonzero count means the machining-time total covers only part of the plan.

totalCuttingLength.description: Sum of cut actions’ cutting lengths, in mm.

minU.description:

stops it. `null` where the far side is open above the upper edge, so that no rim
stands too far right.

the first is the deepest tip the curve places.

below the upper edge, so that no flat is too wide there.

ChamferCurve.description:
What a bevel's surroundings allow a chamfer tool riding it: how deep its tip may sit below
the bevel's lower edge, how wide its flat bottom may be at that depth, and how far its rim
may reach to either side. Every cone a tool matcher accepts for the bevel is read off this.

The picture is the bevel cut straight across, square to its edge: `u` runs across the cut
and `z` up the tool axis, both in mm, with the bevel's lower edge at `u = 0, z = 0`. The
bevel rises to the left, to its upper edge at `z = height`. The face above the upper edge
is the *near side*, on the left; whatever lies past the lower edge is the *far side*, on
the right. Each figure is the nearest obstacle anywhere along the bevel's edge, so this one
cut stands for the whole bevel. `slope` is the bevel's rise over run, a ratio: 1 for a 45°
chamfer.

A chamfer tool is a cone ground to the bevel's angle, described by three numbers: its tip
offset `t`, how far its tip sits below the lower edge; its flat `b`, the diameter of the
flat bottom at its tip, zero for a pointed tool; and its cone height `H`, from the tip up
to the rim, where the cone is widest. Riding the bevel, the cone's near flank lies along
the bevel's own line, so its rim sits at height `H − t`, with its near corner at
`u = −(H − t) / slope` and its far corner at `u = (t + H) / slope + b`. Above the rim the
shaft is no wider than the rim.

The curve admits a tool when three things hold:

- It spans the bevel: its rim sits at or above the upper edge, `H − t >= height`.
- Its flat fits: `b` is at most the widest flat at its tip height `z = −t`. `z` and `flat`
  are parallel, `z` ascending from the deepest tip the curve places to at or below the
  lower edge. For the last `z[i]` at or below the tip height, the widest flat is
  `flat[i] + 2 (z − z[i]) / slope`, widening as the tip rises; no tip sits below `z[0]`.
- Its rim fits: both rim corners lie between `minU` and `maxU`, the near corner at or
  right of `minU` and the far corner at or left of `maxU`.

Every key is always present; a bound nothing sets is `null`.

OffsetLength.description:
An outline a pass follows, measured so that any tool's path length can be read off it.

A pass does not walk the outline: it walks the tool *center*, offset by the tool radius to
the free side, which is shorter than the outline inside a pocket and longer around a boss.
So the length a tool of `radius` travels is `Math.max(0, length + radius * dlDr)`, and zero
means the tool does not fit — the outline is shorter than the tool's own orbit, which a
caller estimating a pass must refuse rather than read as free.

where it reads long by that corner's miter — zero for the filleted corners a pocket that
admits the tool is made of.

necessarily at the bottom. A hole's is on its axis at the top of its wall; a dovetail's

ReachCurve.description:
Surrounding material height as a function of distance from the feature. Material
within `horizontalOffset[i]` rises to `verticalOffset[i]` above the feature. Each
reading is the worst case over the feature's whole surface, measured above each
sampled point.
Both arrays are the same length, ascending, non-negative, in mm. Evaluate the step
function at the first knot whose horizontal offset is at least the query distance;
queries beyond the last knot clamp to it.

The last knot can stand well beyond the others, at the plan-view diagonal of the part and
its fixtures: where material anywhere in the setup stands taller than the nearer offsets
read, that knot carries it, since the spindle face atop a finite holder has to clear it
however far off it stands.

Offsets start at the feature, not the tool axis, and retain no obstacle direction.
For an open feature, the cutter can sit between its contact point and an obstacle.
A cylindrical holder of radius `R` at least as large as the cutting radius `r` reads
the curve at `R + r`: that height is the required stickout before clearances. For example, a
Ø10 cutter with a Ø24 holder reads at 17 mm from the feature, not 7 mm.

![A cutter beside an external wall, with an obstacle beyond the cutter: the holder
footprint extends R + r from the contact point](./media/reach-curve.svg)

Closed features allow an optimization: enclosing material lies beyond the cutting
edge away from the axis, so a holder wider than the cutter reads at `R - r` instead;
a holder narrower than the cutter adds no reach constraint. Tool checks
use this for holes, sinks, non-open pockets, U-slots and threads; potentially open
feature kinds use the conservative `R + r` footprint. The curve can overestimate
holder reach because it has lost obstacle direction; it is not a collision proof.

![A cutter inside a closed pocket, with horizontal offsets measured outward from
its floor and vertical offsets measured upward](./media/reach-curve-closed.svg)

Here the cutter sits inside the pocket. Only the holder's overhang beyond the
cutting edge, `R - r`, extends over the surrounding material.

Shaft checks (neck, shoulder, and shank) read every feature as the closed pocket above, at
`R - r`. Tool checks sweep tapered shaft and holder layers with their heights and
clearances; the cylindrical example above explains the holder footprint. Callers can draw
the curve or sweep an envelope of their own.

get.description:
Requires **Import a tool holder** (`PATCH /v1/holders/{id}`) to have run and its job to have
succeeded.

Returns the derived holder as Autodesk Fusion writes one: millimetres, segments nose-first,
hyphenated keys.

By default this is a **tool library** (`format=library`) that Fusion can import directly.
`format=document` returns the bare holder document the kernel wrote, which carries the same
geometry but cannot be imported on its own.

The exported envelope stops at the gauge plane by default: material above it is inside the
spindle and cannot collide with anything. Pass `trim=false` for the complete envelope,
including the taper. Both are written by the kernel during the import, so neither is a
reshaping of the other. `trim=true` falls back to the complete envelope for a holder that has
no gauge plane to cut at, or whose taper a flip put at the nose.

An unmeasured gauge length is not written as zero. In a library it becomes the sum of every
segment height — Fusion's own idiom for a holder whose geometry is its gauge length; in a
document the field is omitted, which puts Fusion's own field into manual mode.
